title: Usage Guardrails — Interaction Storyboard & Decision Log
summary: Working storyboard and decisions for a unified "guardrails" surface in Console that lets teams preview, simulate, and enforce per-credential and per-route rate limits and quota policies before they go live. Emphasis on a preview/simulate mode, staged enforcement (monitor -> warn -> enforce), cost forecasting, and fast troubleshooting links to per-key breakdowns.
goals: Provide an end-to-end flow for configuring quota and rate-limit policies with minimal surprise to engineering teams
Enable safe rollouts via preview mode and staged enforcement
Surface cost/latency impact of policies using quick simulations
Make debugging and attribution of hits easy (per-key, per-route, per-model)
Reduce support tickets caused by unexpected throttles through clearer microcopy and explainability
user_personas: Platform engineer who manages API keys for internal teams and needs predictable throughput
Growth product engineer who runs experiments and wants quick, reversible throttles for test traffic
Customer success/ops contact who responds to tenant complaints about errors
SRE responsible for global availability and wants graceful degradation paths
storyboard_notes:
Scene 1: Onboarding. Platform engineer lands on a new 'Guardrails' wizard pre-populated with detected keys and routes. Primary CTA: 'Create guardrail'. Secondary: 'Simulate first'.

Scene 2: Quick simulation. An inline 'What-if' slider allows changing e.g., requests/min, burst, and model routing preferences; right-hand pane shows instant estimated token cost, 95th latency impact, and a simulated error-rate curve. Option to run simulated historical replay for last 7 days.

Scene 3: Staged enforcement. Default policy template: Monitor -> Warn -> Enforce. UX shows a timeline with toggle points. When 'Warn' is on, console will send audit events and a configurable Slack/webhook. 'Enforce' shows expected user-facing error codes and suggested fallbacks (e.g., route to smaller model, sample/queue requests).

Scene 4: Live incident flow. When a key approaches its limit, an in-console alert card appears with 'Inspect key' and 'Open mitigation' quick actions. 'Inspect key' opens per-key breakdown with traffic slices and top offending routes. 'Open mitigation' opens a one-click temporary soft-increase with an audit checkbox.

Scene 5: Post-mortem. After enforcement, the console provides a templated report summarizing blocked requests, cost delta, and top 3 devs/teams to notify.
interaction_flows: Configure -> Simulate: create a policy draft, run historical replay, accept or tune parameters
Draft -> Preview: run a 24h forward simulation to show projected token spend and blocked requests
Preview -> Schedule: schedule policy to shift from monitor->warn->enforce with timestamps
Enforcement fallback: on hard-limit, traffic routed to fallback model or queued with exponential backoff
Fast rollback: single-click revert policy that also annotates the rollback with a reason
microcopy_snippets: Monitor: Record events but don't block traffic. Good for initial validation.
Warn: Let traffic through, but send alerts when threshold crossed. Use this before enabling enforcement.
Enforce: Block requests that exceed this policy. Consider adding fallback models to avoid user-visible errors.
Simulate: Run this to see approximate cost and error-rate impact using historical traffic (non-binding).
Blocked response: "Request blocked by usage guardrail. Try again later or contact your admin. Error code: GUARDRAIL_LIMIT"
wireframe_components: Top-level summary card (current spend, 7d forecast, active policies)
Policy timeline widget (monitor -> warn -> enforce toggles with scheduling)
What-if simulator panel (sliders + forecast numbers + simulated chart)
Per-key breakdown drill-in (heatmap by route/time + top N calls)
Audit log w/ quick rollback and annotate buttons
Mitigation quick actions (temporary lift, add fallback model, set sample rate)
Explainability overlay (why this request was blocked: rule, token count, route)
Policy diff view (compare two policy revisions side-by-side)
accessibility_notes: All interactive timeline elements must be keyboard-focusable with clear ARIA labels
Charts must provide table-mode and CSV export for screen-reader users
Color alone must not convey severity: use icons + text labels for Monitor/Warn/Enforce
Modal dialogs that run simulations must announce progress and be cancellable
backlog_actions: Prototype 'historical replay' backend endpoint and wire a toggle on the simulator
Design policy diff UI (mock + accessibility QA)
Add explainability hook: attach the exact rule id and token delta to every blocked response
Integrate Slack/webhook templates for 'Warn' phase alerts
Implement single-click temporary lift with audit annotation
open_questions: Data retention for simulation: how far back can we replay without excessive cost?
How to represent multi-tenant attribution when multiple keys share capacity?
Should preview simulations be exact (replay) or heuristic (fast approx)?
What default thresholds should templates use for new users to minimize support noise?
Do we surface suggested fallback models automatically or leave it manual?
decisions: Adopt staged enforcement by default: Monitor -> Warn -> Enforce; users can skip stages
Simulator will offer two modes: Quick heuristic (instant) and Replay (takes longer, more accurate)
Blocked responses will include a stable rule id and a suggested mitigation string
Expose per-key heatmaps in the first iteration; per-route attribution will be a follow-up
